d.label: How does snow form?
d.question: How does snow form up in the sky?
d.life: Imagine blowing on a cold window and seeing tiny drops of fog appear. Clouds are like that, but far up high where it is very cold.

task.prompt: What do snowflakes start as in the clouds?
task.explain: Snowflakes start as tiny ice crystals that grow bigger as they bump into more water bits!

d.label: Why is each flake different?
d.question: Why does no two snowflake look exactly the same?
d.life: Imagine building a sandcastle where every grain of sand takes a slightly different path to get there. Snowflakes travel through changing air on their way down.

task.prompt: What makes snowflakes end up with different shapes?
options: 🎈 They are blown up like balloons
🌦️ They travel through changing air and temperature
🐟 They copy the shape of fish
task.explain: Each snowflake takes its own path through the air, so its shape changes in its own way!

d.label: How far does snow fall?
d.question: How fast does snow fall to the ground?
d.life: Imagine dropping a feather from your bed and watching it float slowly down. Snowflakes drift down in a similar gentle way.

task.prompt: About how fast does a snowflake fall?
task.explain: Snowflakes usually fall slowly, about as fast as a slow walk, so they can drift down gently!

d.label: Where does snow come from?
d.question: Why does snow only fall in cold places?
d.life: Imagine an ice cube melting on a hot day. Snow needs cold air so it does not melt before it lands.

task.prompt: What keeps snow from melting as it falls?
task.explain: Cold air keeps snowflakes frozen so they can reach the ground as snow!

d.label: Why are flakes six-sided?
d.question: Why are most snowflakes shaped like six-pointed stars?
d.life: Imagine building with blocks that always snap together in groups of six, like the cells of a honeycomb. Snow builds itself in a similar way.

task.prompt: What shape do most snowflakes have?
task.explain: Most snowflakes have six points because of how water freezes into tiny ice crystals!

d.label: Why do flakes fall slowly?
d.question: How can a snowflake float down so slowly?
d.life: Think of a feather drifting down from a pillow instead of a rock dropped from your hand.

task.prompt: What helps snow float down slowly?
options: 🚀 Being shot out of a rocket
task.explain: Snowflakes are light and spread out, so the air pushes back and they drift down slowly!

d.label: How big is a snowflake?
d.question: How big is a typical snowflake?
d.life: Think of the tip of your pinky finger. Could a snowflake be that small or even smaller?

task.prompt: About how wide is a typical snowflake?
task.explain: Most snowflakes are only a few millimeters wide, which is tiny!

d.label: Who photographed snowflakes?
d.question: Who was the first person to photograph a snowflake?
d.life: Imagine a tiny glitter star landing on your mitten. Could a camera catch it before it melts?

task.prompt: Who took the first snowflake photos?
task.explain: Wilson Bentley, a farmer from Vermont, took thousands of snowflake photos!

d.label: Can snow take other shapes?
d.question: Can snowflakes take shapes other than six-pointed stars?
d.life: Imagine soft clay that squishes into different shapes. Snow can change shape too, depending on the air.

task.explain: Snow can make needles, plates, and columns, depending on how cold and wet the air is!

d.label: What builds an ice crystal?
d.question: What tiny pieces build an ice crystal?
d.life: Imagine tiny LEGO bricks snapping together. Each brick is a very small piece of water.

task.prompt: What are ice crystals built from?
task.explain: Water molecules lock together in a neat six-sided pattern as they freeze!

d.label: Why does snow look white?
d.question: Why does snow look white when ice is clear?
d.life: Imagine a pile of broken glass. Each piece is clear, but the whole pile looks bright and white.

options: 🌈 Its ice reflects all colors of light
🍦 It is made of vanilla ice cream
task.explain: The tiny ice pieces scatter all the colors of light, and they mix together into white!
